definition: A question from a customer asking for information.
business_context_example: We answer every enquiry within four working hours.

definition: Real-time text support on a website or app.
business_context_example: Live chat handles three times more contacts than the phone.

definition: The line of customers waiting to speak to someone.
business_context_example: The call queue hit 14 people at lunchtime.

definition: To make a caller wait while you do something.
business_context_example: May I put you on hold for two minutes while I check?

definition: To send a caller to a different person or department.
business_context_example: Before you transfer a call, tell the customer who they'll speak to.

definition: A return call arranged for a later time.
business_context_example: We offer a callback instead of a 15-minute wait.

definition: Outside normal working times.
business_context_example: Out of hours enquiries go to email, not voicemail.

definition: How long a customer waits before being helped.
business_context_example: Average wait time dropped from six minutes to ninety seconds.

definition: How quickly you reply to a customer's first message.
business_context_example: Our response time target is two hours, and we hit it 94% of the time.

definition: Solving the customer's problem in the very first conversation.
business_context_example: First contact resolution matters more to customers than speed.

definition: How long it takes to fully solve a problem.
business_context_example: Resolution time doubles whenever a case needs a third department.

definition: A short questionnaire asking how happy the customer was.
business_context_example: The satisfaction survey is two questions long, on purpose.

definition: The agreed level of service customers can expect.
business_context_example: Our service standard promises a named contact for every complaint.

definition: A customer telling you that something was wrong.
business_context_example: A complaint is information, and most people never bother to give it.

definition: The process of dealing with customer complaints.
business_context_example: Good complaint handling turns angry customers into loyal ones.

definition: To show you have heard and understood the customer.
business_context_example: Acknowledge the problem before you explain the policy.
translation_bg: да призная, да покажа, че съм чул

definition: To show you understand how the customer feels.
business_context_example: Empathise once, sincerely. Three times sounds like a script.

definition: To calm a situation that is becoming angry.
business_context_example: Lowering your voice de-escalates faster than being right.

definition: To accept personal responsibility for solving a problem.
business_context_example: Take ownership even when the mistake was another team's.

definition: To tell customers honestly what will happen and when.
business_context_example: Manage expectations early: three days is fine if you said three days.

definition: To promise less than you can do, then do more.
business_context_example: Say Friday and deliver Wednesday. Under-promise and over-deliver.

definition: A customer who is hard to satisfy or communicate with.
business_context_example: Most difficult customers are simply customers nobody has listened to yet.

definition: To say sorry in a way that sounds real, not automatic.
business_context_example: Apologise sincerely once, then talk about the fix.

definition: Something free given to keep a customer happy, without admitting fault.
business_context_example: We sent a goodwill gesture: a free month, no argument.

definition: To fix a customer's problem completely.
business_context_example: It took two calls to resolve the issue, and she told us so.

definition: A temporary way for the customer to continue while you fix the cause.
business_context_example: Here's a work around for today, and the real fix lands on Thursday.

definition: A new item sent instead of a faulty one.
business_context_example: The replacement went out the same afternoon.

definition: Swapping a product for a different one.
business_context_example: An exchange is possible within 30 days with the receipt.

definition: Evidence that the customer bought the item.
business_context_example: The order number counts as proof of purchase, no paper needed.

definition: A promise to repair or replace a product for a period.
business_context_example: The warranty covers faults, not damage from dropping it.

definition: The rules about sending goods back.
business_context_example: Our returns policy is 30 days, no questions, and it costs us very little.

definition: A code used to follow a delivery.
business_context_example: I'll send the tracking number so you can watch it yourself.

definition: The reference identifying a customer's purchase.
business_context_example: Could you give me your order number, it starts with WT.

definition: A shipment arriving later than promised.
business_context_example: Tell customers about a delayed delivery before they ask.

definition: Not currently available to buy.
business_context_example: The item is out of stock until the 20th, and I can hold one for you.

definition: An order placed for something not yet in stock.
business_context_example: We put it on backorder and told her the honest date.

definition: The person whose name the account is in.
business_context_example: I can only discuss this with the account holder, I'm sorry.

definition: To check that someone is who they say they are.
business_context_example: We verify identity with two details before any change.

definition: A question used to confirm a customer's identity.
business_context_example: The security question is the town where they opened the account.

definition: A collection of articles answering common questions.
business_context_example: Half our tickets are already answered in the knowledge base.

definition: Frequently asked questions and their answers.
business_context_example: We rewrote the FAQ using the exact words customers use.

definition: Letting customers solve problems without contacting staff.
business_context_example: Self-service works when it's genuinely faster, not when it's a wall.

definition: Someone who keeps buying from you over time.
business_context_example: A loyal customer is worth eight new ones, and costs nothing to keep.

definition: A customer who buys again.
business_context_example: Sixty per cent of last month's orders came from repeat customers.

definition: To bring back someone who stopped buying.
business_context_example: We won back a customer by simply admitting what went wrong.

definition: Customers' opinions about your product or service.
business_context_example: Feedback you don't act on is just a survey.

definition: To pass a customer's problem to someone with more authority.
business_context_example: Escalate the case if it isn't solved within 48 hours.
translation_bg: да предам случая на по-високо ниво

definition: The written record of what happened with a customer's issue.
business_context_example: Write case notes as if the next person has never heard of this customer.

definition: To give updates even when there is no solution yet.
business_context_example: Keep the customer informed every 48 hours, even to say nothing changed.

definition: To mark a customer's issue as finished.
business_context_example: Never close a case without asking whether it's actually solved.
